title: Review Litigation Invoice Against Outside Counsel Billing Guidelines — Compliance Deviation Report

blind.coverage: I read all 49 criteria and the instructions. I read four documents in full: the Guidelines v4.2, the engagement letter with Exhibits A and B, the prior approval log, and the transmittal email. I parsed the XLSX invoice with scripts. That covered all 139 fee entries (each hours x rate checked), the 22 expense lines, the Timekeeper Summary, Matter Status, YTD Summary, Rate Schedule and LEDES sheets. I recomputed the figures behind every dollar criterion: Kwan, both block-billing reductions, Tanaka, photocopying, Westlaw, hotel, meals, travel time, the surcharge and the YTD total. I also footed the fee and expense totals. I did no case-law research because no criterion turns on external law; everything depends on the supplied Guidelines. I did not check real ORD-SFO scheduled flight times. The record contains no flight duration, and the finding uses the rubric's own 4h20m figure. The advisor review was rate-limited and did not run.

findings.title: Business-class airfare forced into 'borderline' although the rubric's own 4h20m flight clearly qualifies under §6.1(b)
findings.explanation: Guidelines §6.1 sets a bright line. Flights scheduled under 4 hours must be coach. Flights of 4 hours or more 'may be booked [in business class] without prior approval.' The rubric's own figure is about 4h20m, which is over the line, so under the text the business-class fare is plainly permitted, not borderline. C-020 fails any report that treats the fare as 'clearly compliant.' C-042 fails a report that 'dismisse[s it] as compliant.' That fails the correct reading of §6.1(b). A strong answer might instead say the fare is allowed by class but falls within the unapproved out-of-forum trip under §9.1. The 4h20m figure is also not in the record, so the criteria depend on an outside fact the solver must supply. C-019's framing ('potentially violates... requires coach for under 4 hours') has the same premise, though its fail condition ('not flagged at all') is lenient.

evidence.quote: For domestic flights with a scheduled duration of four (4) hours or more, business class may be booked without prior approval.
FAIL if the report treats the business class airfare as either clearly compliant or clearly non-compliant without noting the borderline nature.
OR if it is entirely dismissed as compliant.

findings.suggested_fix: Accept either (a) a finding that the fare complies with §6.1(b) because the flight is 4 hours or more, with the trip still flagged under §9.1(3), or (b) a request for itinerary confirmation of the scheduled duration. Drop the requirement that it be called 'borderline.'

findings.title: Invoice does not foot: fee entries total $269,554.00, not $242,687.00; Cho's entries total 214.0 hrs/$41,730, not 186.0/$36,270
findings.explanation: Every one of the 139 fee entries in the Professional Fees Detail and LEDES sheets computes correctly (hours x rate), but together they total $269,554.00. The subtotal rows and the Timekeeper Summary say $242,687.00. Seven of eight timekeepers are off; only Kwan matches. Elaine Cho has 23 entries totaling 214.0 hours ($41,730.00), against the 186.0 hours ($36,270.00) stated. The expense lines sum to $244,652.14, not the stated $244,642.14. So the entries total $514,206.14 while the invoice states $487,329.14. C-027 treats $36,270 as the only correct at-risk amount and fails 'materially incorrect' figures. An auditor who sums Cho's entries gets $41,730 and would fail, though that is arguably the more careful answer. No criterion rewards catching this footing error, which is a core deviation in a 'full deviation report.'

evidence.quote: PASS if the report states that $36,270.00 (186.0 hours × $195/hour) is at risk ... FAIL if the amount is materially incorrect or not quantified.

findings.suggested_fix: Either fix the workbook so the entries match the subtotals, or accept Cho at-risk figures of $36,270 (as billed) or $41,730 (per line items) and add credit for spotting the discrepancies between the entries and the stated totals.

findings.title: Requires a three-tier severity taxonomy the instructions never request
findings.explanation: The instructions ask only for 'a full deviation report.' C-041 fails any report that does not sort violations into at least three severity levels like 'Mandatory Reduction / Requires Discussion / Process Failure.' A competent deviation report can be organized by Guideline section, by fees versus expenses, or by line item, with a recommended adjustment and rationale for each item, and never grade severity. Severity tiers are a stylistic choice, not a standard part of an invoice deviation report. The rubric presumably expects them because they matter to C-042, but the solver has no signal to supply them.

evidence.quote: produce a full deviation report. Output: `invoice-compliance-deviation-report.docx`.
FAIL if violations are not categorized by severity.

findings.suggested_fix: Delete C-041, or pass any report that tells clear mandatory reductions apart from items needing discussion or approval, in whatever structure.

findings.title: Oct 28 headcount criterion counts a law student as an 'attorney'; excluding Kwan, attendance equals the cap
findings.explanation: §5.1 limits internal strategy meetings to four attorneys. Kwan is a summer associate and law student (Rate Schedule: 'N/A — Law Student'), not an attorney. Excluding him, exactly four attorneys attended, which meets the limit. Yet C-010 passes a report that says '4 excluding Kwan' attended against a cap of 4, rewarding the flagging of a non-violation. A competent answer might say the headcount limit is met once Kwan's time is disallowed under §3.1, or might say nothing about headcount because Kwan's time is already removed. Either answer sits awkwardly between PASS and FAIL. The note also points to 'C-007' for the attorney-hour issue, which is C-008.

evidence.quote: No more than **four (4) attorneys** may attend any single internal strategy meeting or conference.
B6='Timothy Kwan' | C6='Summer Associate' | D6='N/A — Law Student'
identifies that 5 attorneys (or 4 excluding Kwan) attended ... and the Guidelines §5.1 cap attendance at 4 attorneys

findings.suggested_fix: Pass a report that addresses the attendance limit either way: five attendees over the cap if Kwan is counted, or compliant or moot once Kwan is excluded and disallowed. Fix the C-007 cross-reference.

findings.title: Relativity criterion ignores prior approval Entry No. 4 for third-party Relativity hosting
findings.explanation: The prior approval log's Entry No. 4 approves 'continued use of Relativity-hosted document review platform' through third-party vendor CloudStar at an estimated $12,000–$15,000 a month. §7.1(c) makes third-party vendor charges reimbursable, subject to §9.1. A careful answer may therefore call the $18,500 charge pre-approved in principle, flag the $3,500–$6,500 excess over the estimate, and ask for the vendor invoice. C-017 passes only (a) 'non-reimbursable overhead' or (b) borderline 'because it could be characterized as either substantive e-discovery tool or file storage/overhead.' Its fail condition is only 'not mentioned at all,' so the approved-but-over-estimate answer falls between PASS and FAIL. Option (a) rewards full disallowance, which ignores the documented approval.

evidence.quote: Approval for continued use of Relativity-hosted document review platform for Phase II production. Monthly hosting and processing fees through third-party vendor CloudStar Technologies, LLC.
Monthly hosting fees estimated at \$12,000--\$15,000/month; approved through completion of document review phase.
FAIL if the Relativity charge is not mentioned at all.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a PASS path for treating the charge as approved under PA-004 while flagging the amount over the estimate and asking for vendor backup.

findings.title: 'Failed to provide' 75% notification is premature: this invoice crossed the threshold and the 5-business-day window had not run
findings.explanation: Cumulative spend crosses $2.1M only with this October invoice, dated November 4, 2024 (September YTD was $1,743,612). §10.1 requires notice 'within five (5) business days of the date on which cumulative invoiced fees and expenses reach the 75% threshold,' which is about November 11. On the invoice date the firm had not yet missed the deadline. The invoice's Matter Status sheet also gives a written budget status (79.7% used), though without the required contents. A careful report might say the notice is due or deficient in content rather than 'failed.' A strict judge could fail that under C-030's 'failed to provide' wording.

evidence.quote: This notification must be provided within five (5) business days of the date on which cumulative invoiced fees and expenses reach the 75% threshold.
Year-to-date spend through October 2024: $2,230,941.14. Budget remaining: $569,058.86. Budget utilization: 79.7%.
Blackwell Stanhope failed to provide the required written notification per Guidelines §10.1.

findings.suggested_fix: Pass a report that flags the missing or deficient §10.1 notification: not provided, or due and not yet received, or the budget line lacks the required summary, remaining tasks and revised estimate.

findings.title: Requires concluding the 2024 annual budget is insufficient for work 'through trial in April 2025'
findings.explanation: The $2.8M figure is the 2024 annual budget (engagement letter §7; Guidelines §10.1 set budgets 'for each calendar year'). Work in January–April 2025, including trial, falls under a 2025 budget. The sound concern is that $569,058.86 left for November–December 2024 is thin against October's $487k run rate, with expert reports due December 20. A competent report making exactly that point, without tying the 2024 budget to the April 2025 trial, could fail C-040's conjunctive wording.

evidence.quote: The 2024 annual budget for this Matter is \$2,800,000.00
and that remaining budget is insufficient for the work remaining through trial in April 2025.

findings.suggested_fix: Change it to: discusses cumulative spend against the 75% threshold and whether the remaining 2024 budget is adequate for work through year-end, with optional comment on 2025 and trial.

findings.title: Mandates recommending retroactive/renewed approval for Cho despite Guidelines language making disallowance the stated consequence
findings.explanation: §9.1(6) says failure to renew 'will result in disallowance of all time billed after the expiration date,' and §9.3(b) allows retroactive approval 'only in extraordinary circumstances.' A reviewer acting for VIH can reasonably recommend full disallowance of Cho's October time, perhaps inviting the firm to request renewal for future work. C-044 fails any report without a re-authorization recommendation. Whether to offer retroactive approval is client business judgment, not something a deviation report must contain. The criterion's 'work may have been valuable' premise is also speculation.

evidence.quote: Failure to obtain renewal before the expiration of the approval period will result in disallowance of all time billed after the expiration date.
retroactive approval is not guaranteed and will be granted only in extraordinary circumstances
FAIL if no recommendation is made regarding Cho's re-authorization.

findings.suggested_fix: Pass any report that gives a clear disposition for Cho's post-expiration time: disallow, or disallow pending a retroactive or renewal request.

findings.title: Overage-specific figures required even though the unapproved out-of-forum trip supports full disallowance
findings.explanation: C-018 rightly flags that the San Francisco trip lacked the prior approval §9.1(3) requires. §9.1, §9.3(a) and §11.2(e) allow full disallowance of the associated expenses. A report that recommends disallowing all trip expenses, with the hotel, meals and car issues noted as aggravating, may never compute the $984 hotel or $87.40 meal overages. C-022 and C-033 would then fail it as 'materially incorrect,' even though its adjustment is larger and grounded in the Guidelines. Most strong answers will give both a primary and an alternative figure, so only some competent answers are affected.

evidence.quote: Full disallowance of expenses incurred without required prior approval per §9.1
FAIL if the overage is materially incorrect.

findings.suggested_fix: Also pass a report that recommends full disallowance of the unapproved trip's expenses while noting that each item also exceeds its cap.

findings.title: Record inconsistencies in names (Vanguard vs Saxonbrook; Pryor-Hall vs Pryce-Hall) carried into the criteria
findings.explanation: The client is 'Saxonbrook Industrial Holdings' in the body text but 'VIH' and 'Vanguard Industrial Holdings' in headers, signature blocks and the email domain. The timekeeper is 'Jonathan Pryor-Hall' in the rosters, but narratives say 'J. Pryce-Hall.' Several criteria use 'Pryce-Hall.' There are also inconsistent approval dates: Rosenberg is on the March 2023 engagement roster but the log shows 'May 10, 2024'; for DeVries, Exhibit A says 12/12/2023 and the log says January 15, 2024. Judges will probably tolerate the spelling differences, so grading risk is low. But a thorough report may flag these as identity or record discrepancies, and a criterion that names the wrong spelling adds some noise.

evidence.quote: Saxonbrook Industrial Holdings, Inc. (\"VIH\")
conference with J. Pryce-Hall and R. Tanaka regarding expert discovery strategy
Alicia Rosenberg        Paralegal                             \$195/hour                 May 10, 2024

findings.suggested_fix: Make names and approval dates consistent across the documents and use the roster spelling (Pryor-Hall) in all criteria.

blind.overall: Most of the rubric is sound. I verified the Kwan, block-billing, deposition, photocopying, Westlaw, overhead, hotel, meals, travel-time, Forrest and local-counsel figures against the record, and they are correct. The most serious defect is the business-class airfare set (C-019/C-020/C-042). §6.1(b) expressly allows business class on flights of 4 hours or more, and the rubric's own ~4h20m figure clears that line. So the rubric requires calling the fare 'borderline' and fails the correct 'compliant' reading, under an all-pass metric. Second, the invoice does not foot: fee entries total $269,554.00 against the stated $242,687.00 (Cho 214.0 hrs against 186.0), and expense lines are $10 over their stated total. The rubric ignores this, fixes Cho's at-risk amount at the subtotal figure, and gives no credit for catching the discrepancy. Smaller problems are debatable: a hidden severity-tier requirement (C-041), the Kwan headcount logic (C-010), the Relativity approval gap (C-017), the timing of the 75% notice (C-030), the budget framing that runs the 2024 budget to the 2025 trial (C-040), and a mandated recommendation for Cho (C-044). Some criteria duplicate each other (C-015/C-048, C-016/C-049), which is harmless but redundant.

sol_verdicts.reason: §6.1(b): 'For domestic flights with a scheduled duration of four (4) hours or more, business class may be booked without prior approval.' The rubric's own ~4h20m figure clears that line. C-020 and C-042 fail a report that calls the fare compliant, which is the correct reading. C-019's FAIL condition is only 'not flagged at all'. But its PASS text requires 'potentially violates', so a report that analyzes the fare and finds it compliant may still fail. That makes C-019 arguable.

I re-summed this session: 23 Cho entries total 214.0 hrs / $41,730, but subtotal row G146 and Timekeeper Summary E7/F7 say 186.0 / $36,270. C-027 fails a 'materially incorrect' amount, so a solver who uses the line items fails it. C-026's FAIL applies only if the expiry is not flagged, so it is at risk only when its 186.0 figure is read into PASS. That makes C-026 arguable.

C-038 tests only internal consistency: the total must equal the sum of the listed adjustments. The footing error does not affect that. C-039 fixes the base at the stated $487,329.14. The line items actually total $514,206.14. A report that declines to give a final payable figure until the firm corrects the invoice, or computes from the line-item base, could fail. Most reports will use the stated total, so C-039 is arguable, not problematic.

The engagement letter says 'The 2024 annual budget for this Matter is $2,800,000.00'. §10.1 ties the revised estimate to 'the remainder of the calendar year.' C-040's PASS requires saying the remaining budget is insufficient 'through trial in April 2025.' That treats the 2024 budget as covering 2025 work, which is a wrong premise. The misgrade depends on the judge reading PASS conjunctively, because the FAIL clause is lenient.

C-041 requires at least three severity tiers. The instructions never ask for that, and a deviation report organized by section or line item is standard. C-046 asks for Guideline section citations, which are implicit in a guidelines deviation report. Its 75% threshold is a grading tolerance, and it absorbs the §3.1/§9.1 overlap for Cho and Kwan.

§4.2 says VIH 'reserves the right' to reduce by 30%, and §11.2(b) lists that reduction as a remedy. Recommending the available remedy is the reviewer's job, and C-037 asks for recommended adjustments. A report that makes the 30% reduction conditional on itemization still applies it and states the figure. The arithmetic ($1,276.50; $1,557.30) is correct.

The October invoice dated Nov 4 is what crosses the $2.1M threshold (September YTD was $1,743,612). §10.1 allows 'five (5) business days of the date on which cumulative invoiced fees and expenses reach the 75% threshold.' So 'failed to provide' is premature on the invoice date. A report that says 'due / not yet received' could be failed by a strict judge.

The transmittal has a 'Matter Status Summary' and a 'Looking Ahead' section. It lacks the §10.1 content: 'key drivers of cost', necessity, and 'expected trajectory of spending'. A report calling the explanation absent or deficient flags the gap and passes. The criterion's wording is slightly loose, but no competent answer fails because of it.

C-009 already computes the overage excluding Kwan (15.2 hours, 11.2 over the cap). It requires only some specific dollar reduction, with no fixed figure, so overlap with the Kwan disallowance is left to the solver. C-038 checks only that the total equals the sum of the parts. Neither fails a report that avoids double-counting.

§6.1 says black car services are 'not reimbursable under any circumstances,' and full disallowance passes C-024. The alternative taxi-equivalent path is lenient but reflects client discretion ('VIH may apply' remedies, §11.2). It fails no correct answer.

The record itself alternates between Pryor-Hall and Pryce-Hall, and each criterion identifies the entry clearly by date, hours and tasks. LLM judges will not fail a report over the spelling. No correct answer changes.

findings.title: Business-class airfare must be called 'borderline' although §6.1(b) plainly permits it on a ≥4h flight (rubric says ~4h20m)
findings.explanation: §6.1 is a bright line. Flights scheduled under 4 hours fly coach, and business class 'may be booked without prior approval' on flights of 4 hours or more. The rubric's own ~4h20m figure clears the line. C-020 fails a report that treats the fare as 'clearly compliant.' C-042 fails a report where the fare is 'entirely dismissed as compliant.' Both would fail the correct reading. A strong answer finds the cabin class compliant and still flags the whole trip as unapproved out-of-forum travel under §9.1(3) (C-018). The 4h20m figure is not in the record, so the criteria also depend on an outside fact. With all-pass scoring, this alone can zero out a correct report.

evidence.quote: For domestic flights with a scheduled duration of four (4) hours or more, business class may be booked without prior approval.
FAIL if the report treats the business class airfare as either clearly compliant or clearly non-compliant without noting the borderline nature.
OR if it is entirely dismissed as compliant.

findings.suggested_fix: Accept either (a) cabin class compliant under §6.1(b) because the flight is 4 hours or more (optionally subject to itinerary confirmation), with the trip flagged under §9.1, or (b) a request to verify the scheduled duration. Drop the mandatory 'borderline' label.

findings.title: C-019 frames the business-class fare as a 'potential violation' even though the rubric's own flight time complies
findings.explanation: C-019's FAIL condition is lenient ('not flagged at all'). But its PASS text says the fare 'potentially violates' §6.1 and requires noting the borderline 4h20m duration. A report that analyzes the fare and concludes it complies with §6.1(b) arguably 'flags' it. A judge reading PASS literally could still fail it. The premise is the same as in O1, with lower misgrade risk.

evidence.quote: potentially violates Guidelines §6.1, which requires coach/economy for domestic flights under 4 hours. The report should note that the Chicago-to-San Francisco flight is approximately 4 hours and 20 minutes, making it a borderline case.

findings.suggested_fix: PASS if the report addresses the business-class fare against §6.1, whatever its conclusion.

findings.title: C-026 hard-codes the 186.0-hour figure, and C-039 fixes the revised total's base at the stated total, despite the footing error

final.changes_from_blind:
1. Upgraded C-041 (severity tiers) from arguable to problematic. The requirement is plainly hidden and fails common competent structures under all-pass scoring. Sol concurs.
2. Upgraded C-040 from arguable to problematic, on the wrong-fact prong: the 2024 annual budget does not govern work through an April 2025 trial. The misgrade depends on a conjunctive reading of PASS.
3. Split blind O1 by status. C-020 and C-042 stay problematic. C-019 is now a separate arguable finding because its FAIL clause is lenient.
4. Split blind O2. C-027 is problematic (re-summed this session: Cho 214.0 hrs / $41,730). C-026 and C-039 are arguable.
5. Removed C-038 and C-047 from the footing finding. C-038 checks only internal consistency, and C-047 correctly states the stated total.
6. Removed C-018 and C-024 from the full-disallowance finding (now O11), leaving C-022 and C-033.
7. Dropped blind O10 (Pryor-Hall/Pryce-Hall, Vanguard/Saxonbrook, Rosenberg/DeVries approval dates). None of these changes a correct answer, and judges will not penalize the spelling.
8. After reading Sol, I rejected its C-046, C-005/C-029, C-031, C-009/C-038, C-024 and naming-drift points as not defects. I adopted no new criteria from Sol.
final.overall:
The rubric is mostly sound, and I confirmed its core dollar figures against the record: Kwan, block billing, deposition, photocopying, Westlaw, overhead, hotel, meals, travel time. Four defects can zero out a correct report under all-pass scoring:
- C-020 and C-042 require calling a business-class fare 'borderline' although §6.1(b) expressly permits it on the rubric's own ~4h20m flight.
- C-027 fixes Cho's at-risk amount at a $36,270 subtotal that the invoice's own 23 line entries contradict ($41,730). The invoice fails to foot overall by $26,877.
- C-041 imposes a hidden three-tier severity taxonomy.
- C-040 requires treating the 2024 annual budget as covering work through an April 2025 trial.

Lesser, arguable issues: C-019, C-026/C-039 (footing), C-010 (Kwan headcount), C-017 (Relativity prior approval), C-030 (notification timing), C-044 (mandated Cho re-authorization) and C-022/C-033 (the full-disallowance alternative). Of Sol's findings, I agree on the airfare, Cho, budget and severity issues. I reject C-046, C-005/C-029, C-031, C-009/C-038, C-024 and the naming-drift point as not defects.
